; Three public JMP entries: select music (A), select an effect (A), and advance audio once.
; Bank 8 must occupy $8000; music/effect data at $A000 need their matching bank. These are
; CPU aliases, not permanent ROM identities.
; A selects a two-byte pointer at $8C00. Disable APU channels, copy eight stream-pointer
; bytes to $C2..C9, reset four note timers, then enable the four tonal/noise channels. Clear
; effect ownership and initialize cached pulse/noise volume.
; Ignore a new effect while either effect channel owns hardware. Otherwise set ownership
; bits 7/6 and copy two stream pointers from the effect directory at $B840 into $E8..EB;
; clear their timers. A is the effect index, doubled for the directory.
; Pulse 1 is a bytecode stream at (Pulse1Stream), with a timer in $DA. A note packs pitch in the
; upper nibble and duration in the lower nibble. Duration is the shared base shifted by bits
; 0..2, plus half that value when bit 3 is set. Notes fetch a period pair through (Pulse1Periods).
; Upper nibbles C..F dispatch controls: envelope/sweep, duration base, absolute stream jump,
; saved return, stream call, stop/rest, or period-table selection. Stream calls save one
; return pointer, not a nesting stack. Commit Y to the stream pointer only after processing
; the event. Envelope bit 4 selects direct volume; otherwise the envelope table supplies a
; held countdown and volume step.
; Commit pulse 1 volume and tick its timers, then decode pulse 2 using the same event
; grammar as pulse 1. Pulse 2 uses $C4/$D4 and $DB. Always update the cached hardware image;
; suppress live pulse 2 writes when an effect owns it (ownership bit 7). The envelope and
; duration calculations mirror pulse 1.
; Commit pulse 2 envelope state, then decode triangle events through (TriangleStream). Triangle notes
; write a period pair through (TrianglePeriods) and set the length-load bit. Controls share stream
; jump/call/return and duration semantics, but configure the linear counter instead of a
; pulse envelope. $DC counts remaining note ticks.
; Decode noise stream (NoiseStream), with duration in $DD. Notes select an envelope position from
; the upper nibble; control events share the stream flow and duration grammar. Period
; selection uses the lower nibble directly. Cache noise registers even while an effect owns
; noise (ownership bit 6); advance the stream after consuming an event.
; Choose fixed or table-stepped noise volume, cache it, and write hardware only when noise
; is not reserved by an effect. Tick the music noise timer before proceeding to effects.
; Decode the pulse effect stream (PulseEffectStream), which temporarily owns pulse 2. This smaller grammar
; supports envelope/sweep, duration base, stop and period-table selection. Effects have
; independent duration/envelope state. A stop holds the stream on its stop token and sets
; bit 7 of the release flags; hardware restoration occurs below when its duration expires.
; Only advance the noise effect while ownership bit 6 is set. Otherwise proceed directly to
; channel restoration.
; Decode noise effects from (NoiseEffectStream), with their own duration base and envelope position. A
; stop sets release bit 6 and holds the token. The effect writes live noise period and
; volume; the music register image remains available for restoration.
; When pulse-effect stop was seen and its timer reaches zero, clear only ownership bit 7 and
; restore all four pulse 2 registers from the music cache. Preserve noise-effect ownership.
; When noise-effect stop was seen and its timer reaches zero, clear only ownership bit 6 and
; restore all four noise registers from the cached music image. Preserve pulse-effect
; ownership.
; Return after music/effect updates and any channel restoration.
